name: The sons of God and the giants
charge: The sons of God, the lineage of Adam, taking wives of the daughters of men of the other nations
summary: The men who multiplied on the face of the earth were of the other nations, not of Adam’s direct line; the sons of God are the lineage of Adam in Genesis 5, the line through Seth, and the daughters of men came out of Cain’s line. The law against marrying the nations was already known. They took wives of whichever they chose, dwelt in the city Cain had built and learned his ways, and the giants were born of that mixing. These are the angels who did not keep their first estate, reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day.
offenseFull: The men who began to multiply on the face of the earth were of the other nations; they were not the direct descendants of Adam. The sons of God are the lineage of Adam laid out in chapter five, the line through Seth, and that is the distinction between the sons of God and the daughters of men (Genesis 5:1-3; Genesis 6:1-2; Luke 3:38). The daughters of men came out of Cain’s line: of Cain his mother said she had gotten a man from the Lord, a man and not a son of God, and the likeness and image of Adam are recorded only of Seth (Genesis 4:1; Genesis 5:3). Cain had built a city, and the sons of God went and dwelt in it and learned of him, which is the same thing happening now.

The law against marrying into the other nations began here in Genesis. It was already known, and Moses had to say it over again to the children of Israel when they came over Jordan, that they were not to make marriages with them, for they turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Seeing that the daughters of men were fair, they took wives of all which they chose (Genesis 6:2). The giants came of the sons of God intermingling with the other nations, and the children born to them became the mighty men of renown: renowned for the fame and the power, and mighty in the wickedness they did, which is the same double sense given to Nimrod as a mighty hunter (Genesis 6:4). Ecclesiasticus says the old giants fell by trusting their own strength and foolishness, and Baruch says their stature and their skill in war gave them neither wisdom nor deliverance (Ecclesiasticus 16:7; Baruch 3:26-28).
judgmentFull: The Lord said his spirit would not always strive with man, and cut man’s days to a hundred and twenty years; the lifespans of chapter five fall away through the generations of Shem, five hundred, then four hundred, then two hundred, down past a hundred and nineteen with Nahor (Genesis 6:3; Genesis 11:10-25). The angels who did not keep their first estate are these same men. Another word for angel is messenger; they came out of the lineage of Adam, and their first estate was sons of God. They left their own habitation, and the Most High has reserved them in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day (Jude 1:6; 2 Peter 2:4).

The wickedness born of that mixing spread until every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was only evil continually and the earth was filled with violence, and it was for Cain’s cause that the earth was drowned (Genesis 6:5, 11; Wisdom of Solomon 10:4). Noah was himself one of the sons of God, and out of all of them in that generation he was the one who did not mingle; he kept the righteousness passed down from Seth and took a wife of his own kindred, as all the fathers from the beginning did (Genesis 6:9; Tobit 4:12). The judgment here is not only the flood. It is a captivity: a whole order of men who had the first estate of sons of God, held in chains against a day of judgment, for a thing that began with the choice of a wife.

text.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.
Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.
And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.
And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.
He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.
Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them:
But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.
And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.
These are the generations of Shem: Shem was an hundred years old, and begat Arphaxad two years after the flood:
And Shem lived after he begat Arphaxad five hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Arphaxad lived five and thirty years, and begat Salah:
And Arphaxad lived after he begat Salah four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Salah lived thirty years, and begat Eber:
And Salah lived after he begat Eber four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg:
And Eber lived after he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu:
And Peleg lived after he begat Reu two hundred and nine years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug:
And Reu lived after he begat Serug two hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nahor:
And Serug lived after he begat Nahor two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
And Nahor lived nine and twenty years, and begat Terah:
And Nahor lived after he begat Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.
For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value.
These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.

Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
